description: Hi! We are an existing team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are working on the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. We are looking for passionate team members interested in coding, web development, game design, and space exploration. If you are interested in joining our team and contributing to an exciting software project, feel free to contact us through this platform.
summary:
ASTROCOMMAND is an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed to make space science engaging through game-based learning.

Young learners explore astronaut training, lunar and Martian outpost operations, space survival and rocket-launch activities. Players manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food and power while protecting astronauts from radiation risks and responding to simulated emergencies.

The platform combines interactive learning activities, mission briefings, resource-management challenges and space exploration simulations. It helps children understand the challenges of living and working in space through hands-on gameplay.

ASTROCOMMAND aims to encourage curiosity, scientific thinking, problem-solving and interest in space exploration.
details:
ASTROCOMMAND is a browser-based educational space mission simulation game developed using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript.

The platform provides interactive learning experiences through astronaut training, lunar and Martian outpost missions, space survival activities and rocket-launch simulation.

Players take the role of mission commanders and manage oxygen, water, food, power, radiation protection and habitat safety. They encounter simulated emergencies such as solar storms, power failures, dust storms, water leaks and equipment problems. They must make decisions to protect their crew and maintain their outpost.

The mission-control dashboard displays resource gauges, mission progress, emergency events and a resource-history chart. The game includes mission briefings, seven-day mission challenges, scoring and educational debriefs.

The rocket-launch experience introduces learners to rocket preparation, countdown procedures, liftoff and spacecraft navigation.

The project uses HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Chart.js and browser Local Storage. It runs in a modern web browser without requiring a backend or API keys.

ASTROCOMMAND makes space-science concepts accessible through visual learning, interactive activities and game-based challenges. It encourages curiosity, decision-making, problem-solving and interest in science and space exploration.

All resource values, consumption rates and event outcomes are simplified educational game settings, not real NASA operational limits or live NASA mission data.
